title: Gemini 4 Carbon & Lean 4 Prove Hadwiger’s 3D Covering Conjecture
whyItMatters: Proved the 70-year-old 3D Hadwiger covering conjecture (every compact 3D convex body can be covered by 8 smaller copies)—discovered by Gemini 4 Carbon and verified in 13,663 lines of Lean 4.
summary: Dror Aiger, Sariel Har-Peled, and Goran Žužić posted a self-contained proof resolving Hadwiger’s 1957 covering / Boltyanski illumination conjecture in three dimensions, lowering the general upper bound from 14 to the optimal 8. Discovered via an experimental Google harness atop Gemini 4 Carbon with minimal human steering, the complete proof is formalized in 13,663 lines of Lean 4 across 34 files against an 18-line standalone specification.
technicalHighlights: Unconditionally proved c(K) ≤ 8 for every compact 3D convex body without symmetry assumptions (improving Prymak’s bound of 14).
Combines John’s position, Cauchy’s planar perimeter formula, shadow-boundary curve variation, and Helly’s theorem in ℝ³.
Completely verified in 13,663 lines of Lean 4 with Mathlib using only standard axioms, checked against an 18-line specification.
caveats: Unrefereed v1 arXiv preprint; author-reported Lean/Comparator audits await independent community replay, and higher dimensions (d ≥ 4) remain open.

scoreRationale.foundational: Settled a classic 69-year-old conjecture in convex and discrete geometry (3D case).
scoreRationale.ripple: First headline research theorem publicly proved and Lean-formalized by Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon model.
scoreRationale.verification: 13,663-line Lean 4 proof checked against an 18-line standalone statement; independent replay still pending.
scoreRationale.velocity: Both the geometric proof and full Lean formalization were synthesized via an experimental Gemini 4 Carbon harness.
